title: The Miami and Fort Lauderdale garnishee over a contract clause
summary: A hidden clause barred playing Fort Lauderdale near Miami; a deputy tries to tie up his money and bus, but a lawyer says the bus cannot be seized.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Managers, bookers and the business of getting work

blocks.x: That was before the In The Mood days. That must have been around fifty six or seven; somewhere along in there. We started on this tour and sure enough, we opened in Miami and it was during that area in the south, in Florida, all the

(inaudible) very close together. I made a little circle around and I played Miami the second time, and this time when I played I was supposed to go to Ft. Lauderdale and by reading some little print, it was in the contract that I wasn't supposed to play the area so many days before, and I frankly hadn't noticed it, but it was plainly in there when I did see it.

In Miami, it was just very fortunate I was my road man myself, and just before intermission, the contract was on to pay during intermission, but I had picked up my money and so this time that it closed, a deputy presented a garnishee to tie up my money for that engagement and they had it written out what part of the contract I was supposed to pay and they received a deposit of money from there and wasn't supposed to play here, that close. (Inaudible). He said you better be glad you got your money, and I said what and he said look here. So then we looked and (inaudible).

This guy then said well, I'll tell you what, I guess we'll just have to tie up your bus, and the proprietor of this place said you better learn a little something about law, you tried but I don't think you can get away with it. And sure enough, they attempted, but I saw an attorney and they said let them tie it up, but if they do, they better turn it loose mighty fast. He said that's your living. How can you make anything and if you owe him something, demand you to pay or sue you or something, but they can't take away how you make your money.
They really attempted to, but they served the papers or something, this attorney had some kind of statement there saying you better not.
Who instituted this proceeding, the guy in Ft. Lauderdale?

I got hold of him, but Burns was one of these--he had this little office in New Orleans and he didn't advertise me as from Oklahoma, as exciting New Orleans style and sometimes I got a hold of him in New Orleans, but I have to say this, he did a terrific job in booking, because not having something that somebody is asking for, he was impressing--

I finally got a hold of him and he said, yeah, I remember that, forget about it. If he wants another date, tell him I'll contact him and he can have another date and if he advertises or something, I'll pay for that from my commission.
I didn't right then because it was too close and Burns had gone on and he had me on another date that I had to go on.
Yeah, yeah. I went on but I did finally come back and played Ft. Lauderdale and everything was fine.
